subject: Re: Availability slots, response ladders & pricing
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@vantagehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vantage Health Procurement <procurement@vantagehealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Inquiry: enterprise coverage & pricing for critical workflows

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We’re evaluating Redwood for a set of clinical inference endpoints that are part of our patient triage workflows. A few items the procurement and engineering team asked me to confirm before we move to commercial: 

- Target availability: we’re looking at options across 99.9 / 99.95 / 99.99 — how do you price each band and what’s the real expected downtime per month for each?
- Response windows: what are typical response SLAs for P1/P2/P3? Can you support 24/7 P1 on-call?
- Escalation coverage: we need named escalation contacts and guarantees for outside business hours; is that an add-on or included?
- Credits & measurement: how are service credits calculated? Is it pro-rata and based on per-minute or per-incident?

Also, procurement asked for an example SOW and rough pricing for a committed 12-month reserved capacity (we estimate 150k tokens/day today, spiking to 500k/day during peak launches).

Could you send a short pricing packet and a draft SOW we can circulate? If possible, include an option that has a lower up-front commitment but higher unit price (we may want an initial ramp).

Appreciate a crisp one-pager — we’re trying to consolidate vendor answers by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Olivia Park
Head of Engineering, Platform
Vantage Health

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@vantagehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-12T12:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: enterprise coverage & pricing for critical workflows

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a short pricing packet and a draft SOW (see attachments). High-level notes below so you have something to share with procurement immediately.

Summary / proposed structure (attached: redwood-support-bundles-v2.pdf, SOW-draft-VG.pdf):

- Availability "slots": same concept as tiers but framed as named slots we can commit to. Example slots: Slot S (99.9), Slot A (99.95), Slot P (99.99). Each slot has a monthly uptime target and an associated monthly fee.
- Response ladders (P1/P2/P3): we map severity -> response time -> remediation target. Out-of-the-box definitions:
  - P1 (production — outage impacting >10%): 15m response, 2 hour mitigation target (Slot P can improve response to 10m).
  - P2 (degradation — partial impact): 1 hour response, fix/workaround in 8 hours.
  - P3 (non-critical): 4 hour response, SLAs handled during business hours.
- On-call & escalation: 24/7 named on-call is an add-on (we can provide rotation, paging, and escalation to an on-site SOC engineer). We offer two models: a retainer-based on-call add-on (flat monthly) or a per-incident escalation fee.
- Credits: credits are pro-rata based on minutes of breach versus the uptime window; formula is in the packet but we can make it more conservative per your needs. Measurements are from our telemetry endpoint (per-route metrics) with mutually agreed instrumentation and runbooks.
- Discounts: standard committed-capacity discounts apply by tier; we can do a first-year onboarding discount for a 12-month reservation.

A few quick clarifying Qs that will change pricing materially:
1) Are the 150k/500k token numbers steady-state or bursty (what % of traffic is spiky)?
2) Do you need per-route pinned models (which affects reserved GPU costs) or can we use routing across shared capacity?

I’ve looped in Karthik for a concrete price matrix and Lauren for SOW edits / procurement coordination. If you want, we can run a short 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the packet.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- redwood-support-bundles-v2.pdf (pricing summary, SLA terms, credit formula)
- SOW-draft-VG.pdf (starter SOW, deliverables, milestones)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@vantagehealth.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-13T15:20:00-08:00
Subject: Pricing proposal — availability slots, response ladders & on-call options

Hi Olivia / Mina,

Following Mina’s note, here’s a compact proposal you can present to procurement. Numbers below are indicative; we’ll finalize in the SOW once we agree on traffic profile and model pinning.

Option 1 — Reserved (12 months, committed capacity):
- Slot S (99.9): $6,000 / month — P1: 30m response, P2: 4h, P3: 8h. Credits: 5% monthly credit per 60m breach.
- Slot A (99.95): $12,500 / month — P1: 15m response, P2: 1h, P3: 4h. Credits: 7.5% monthly credit per 60m breach.
- Slot P (99.99): $32,000 / month — P1: 15m response (can be tightened to 10m with on-call add-on), P2: 30m, P3: 2h. Credits: 10% monthly credit per 30m breach.

On-call / Escalation add-on (optional):
- Retainer model: $10,000 / month — 24/7 named rotation, escalation to senior engineer, twice-per-year war-room support included. Adds formalized post-incident reviews and a dedicated Slack channel.
- Per-incident model: $2,500 / P1 incident beyond agreed thresholds.

Discounts / special terms:
- 12-month commit: standard listed above.
- For a 12-month commit + upfront payment: additional 10% off monthly fees.
- For first-year pilots <6 months: we can offer a one-time 15% pilot discount (applicable only to first 3 months).

Credits & measurement:
- We report per-route uptime from our telemetry. Credits are pro-rata by minute using agreed measurement windows. We’re open to a joint telemetry review window for disputed incidents.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Pick target slot for critical routes (suggest Slot A for most production workflows, Slot P for patient-facing critical endpoints).
2) Decide on on-call model. If you want 10m P1 for Slot P we’ll require the retainer.
3) Sign the SOW and DocuSign link (see related links) so we can lock pricing and schedule onboarding.

I’ve attached the SOW draft with placeholders for QPS, token estimates, and pinning preferences.

Happy to jump on a call — Mina, can you propose 30 minutes this week with Olivia & procurement?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pricing proposal — availability slots, response ladders & on-call options

Thanks Karthik / Mina — this is helpful and gives procurement what they need to start a term sheet. A couple of asks / counterpoints from our side before we lock: 

- Cost split for on-call: our preferred approach is to split the retainer 50/50 for the first 6 months as we build runbooks and playbooks together. After that we can revisit (Vantage covers 50% initially). Can you confirm you’ll accept that for onboarding?
- P1 response for Slot P: we’d like the guaranteed response tightened to 10m (noted you said "can be tightened to 10m with on-call add-on"); if we take the retainer and split cost as above, can you confirm 10m P1 will be contractual?
- Credits: procurement wants credits to be pro-rata and calculated per-minute, not only per-hour buckets. Also would like a max cap on monthly credits (e.g., not exceed 100% of monthly fee).
- Measurement: we prefer a joint telemetry window for disputed incidents and request that Redwood expose the raw per-route uptime CSV for review on request.

If you can update the SOW with those three changes (cost-split clause, 10m P1 for Slot P with retainer, credits per-minute with a cap) we can review internally and aim to sign as early as next week.

I’m happy to do a quick call to finalize — Tue 2026-11-17 09:00 PT works for me.

Best,
Olivia Park
Head of Engineering, Platform
Vantage Health
